title: Fibre bundles and the medium Whitney embedding theorem
summary: Locally trivial fibre bundles with fibre F (Definition 14.2) and examples; Whitney's embedding theorem in the medium version (Theorem 15.1): using Sard's theorem to project a compact n-manifold embedded in R^N down to R^{2n+1}.

objectives.description: Construct fibre-bundle charts for frame and projective bundles, and distinguish fibre bundles from arbitrary surjective submersions.
Prove the compact Whitney embedding bound 2n+1 by avoiding secant and tangent directions.
Explain the immersion bound 2n and why the same projection argument does not prove embedding in 2n.

preparation.description: Read lecture 13: §14 fibre bundles, Definition 14.2 and examples.
Read lecture 14: §15 Theorem 15.1 (Whitney embedding theorem, medium version) with proof.

activities.title: Lecture and exact source reading
activities.instructions: Work through the prepared lecture together with its named source sections. Reconstruct the displayed derivations before looking back. The source reading is part of this unit, including the proof obligations identified in the notes.

activities.title: Problem sheet and discussion
activities.instructions: Write an independent attempt at each problem. Use one hint at a time if needed; preserve the original attempt and record what assistance changed. Explain the hypotheses aloud before requesting a step check.

activities.title: Return without the scaffolding
activities.instructions: After a gap, reconstruct the central argument without notes and revisit the transfer or synthesis problem. Compare against your previous work only afterwards. Record what remains unresolved; reading or recall alone does not certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to sample the listed objectives. Give an independent account of the main theorem and its hypotheses, and solve the transfer/synthesis task. An accepted single exercise is evidence only for its tested capabilities, not whole-unit mastery.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Every surjective submersion is a fibre bundle.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The submersion theorem is local around a point of the total space. A bundle chart must trivialize the entire inverse image of a base neighbourhood.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The frame-to-plane map has all injective matrices as a fibre.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Its fibre over a fixed k-plane is the space of bases of that plane, GL(k). All injective matrices form the total space.
